title: fix: handle invalid JSON responses in CouchDB handlers
notes: Closed without merging or a human code review, so nothing on the PR gives away the findings. The fix itself is sound; the defects are in its tests and in how the 502 is sent.

baseline.notes: The runs the key and its min/max/average figures were drawn from, and what they ran with. Hardcoded here because these runs predate the `versions` field in run.json.

code-review.notes: `severity` is what OCR gave the finding: the most common across the runs that reported it, the higher one on a tie. `required` includes correct findings whose comment failed to post in some runs (e.g. 502-inherits-upstream-headers); when scoring a run, only posted comments count. `extra_credit` holds correct findings a review earns credit for but isn't marked down for missing.

required.summary: The new routing.spec.js tests exercise an inline copy of the proxyForAuth handler, never the real one in api/src/routing.js, so they would still pass if the fix were reverted.
required.match: Says the tests don't load or run the real routing.js handler. Only pointing out that `routing` and `proxyForAuthHandler` are unused is not a match: that is routing-spec-unused-vars.

required.summary: infodoc.spec.js assigns recordDocumentWrite/recordDocumentWrites stubs onto the controller's own exports, but the controller calls the @medic/infodoc library, so the stubs are never invoked and the success-path tests can't pass as intended.
required.match: Says the stubs are on the wrong object, so the code under test never calls them. Only saying they should use sinon.stub so sinon.restore() undoes them is not a match: that is infodoc-stubs-not-restored.

required.summary: infodoc.spec.js replaces recordDocumentWrite/recordDocumentWrites by plain assignment rather than sinon.stub, so afterEach's sinon.restore() never undoes it and the replacement leaks into later specs in the same mocha run.
required.match: Says the assignments are never restored. Saying it overwrites @medic/infodoc is a match too, though wrong in detail: the assignments land on the controller's exports.

required.summary: The 502 is hand-written with res.status(502).json({ error, details }) instead of the serverUtils error helpers used elsewhere in the same handler, so it lacks the `code` field and Accept-based content negotiation of the API's standard error envelope.
required.match: Points at serverUtils (error/serverError/writeJSON) or the API's standard error shape as what the 502 should use.

required.summary: copyProxyHeaders has already copied the upstream status message and headers (including Content-Type) onto res before the parse fails, and res.json() keeps an existing Content-Type, so the JSON 502 goes out labelled as e.g. text/html.
required.match: Says the 502 response carries the upstream's headers or Content-Type.

required.summary: Logging a 100-character preview of the unparseable upstream body could put sensitive data in the logs.
required.match: Says the logged body preview could expose sensitive data. A comment only about the log level or format is not a match.

required.summary: The infodoc.spec.js test claiming to record only successful writes from a partial bulk response asserts only that the bulk stub was called, never which ids it got, so forwarding the failed doc too would still pass.
required.match: Says the partial-bulk test doesn't check which ids were recorded, so it can't tell that the failed doc was filtered out. The same point about the other tests is weak-test-assertions.

required.summary: When the body can't be parsed, infodoc skips the metadata update even if the write succeeded, leaving infodocs stale; log at a higher level.
required.match: Says a successful write can go unrecorded in the infodocs when its response can't be parsed.

required.summary: infodoc.spec.js tests assert only that a stub was called, or only the log template, not the ids or message passed (e.g. the chunked-data and bulk-write tests, and 'should log error with status code and error message').
required.match: Says an infodoc.spec.js test other than the partial-bulk one asserts only that something was called, or only part of what was logged, not the arguments it claims to check.

required.summary: `routing` and `proxyForAuthHandler` in routing.spec.js are declared but never assigned or used.
required.match: Says `routing` and/or `proxyForAuthHandler` are declared but never assigned or used. A finding that goes on to say the tests never run the real handler is routing-tests-copy-handler, and also matches this.

required.summary: The try/catch around JSON.parse is duplicated between routing.js and infodoc.js; extract a shared helper.
required.match: Says the parse-and-catch logic is duplicated across routing.js and infodoc.js, or suggests a shared helper for it.

extra_credit.summary: A body of `null` is valid JSON, so it skips the catch, and `body.id` then throws a TypeError in infodoc.js, the same class of crash the PR is fixing.
extra_credit.match: Says a body that parses to null (or another non-object) gets past the catch and throws on `body.id`.

extra_credit.summary: The early return on parse failure skips audit.expressCallback, so the request leaves no audit entry.
extra_credit.match: Says the early return on a parse failure skips audit.expressCallback, so the request isn't audited.

extra_credit.summary: The handler always responds 502, discarding a meaningful upstream status (e.g. 403/404) that came with a non-JSON body.
extra_credit.match: Says the upstream status code is replaced by 502 and should be passed through when meaningful. Comments about the 502's body or headers are 502-bypasses-serverutils or 502-inherits-upstream-headers.

requirements.notes: Reports split and merge requirements differently from run to run, so each expected requirement is matched by meaning, and one report item may cover several. `status` is the bucket it should land in; `acceptable` lists other buckets that are not counted as a miss. `preconditions_to_confirm` holds the operational facts the skill should list under 'Preconditions to confirm'; empty means it should say None.

required.summary: infodoc.js catches the JSON.parse failure, logs a warning with the upstream status code and error message, and returns early without recording an infodoc write.
required.match: A Delivered item saying infodoc.js catches the parse failure, logs it and skips the infodoc write. Separate items for the catch, the log and the early return together match.

required.summary: routing.js catches the JSON.parse failure in the proxyForAuth handler and logs an error with the status code, error message and a 100-character body preview.
required.match: A Delivered item saying routing.js catches the parse failure and logs it with the status, error and body preview.

required.summary: routing.js responds 502 with error details on a parse failure, returning early so no second response is sent.
required.match: A Delivered item for the 502 response and the early return. Pending verification matches only when it names the upstream headers / Content-Type copied onto res (see code-review 502-inherits-upstream-headers).

required.summary: An invalid upstream response no longer leaves the request hanging: both handlers now finish (routing.js by responding, infodoc.js by returning from a side-effect handler).
required.match: A Delivered item saying the request completes instead of hanging, or the 502 and early-return items when no separate item covers it. Pending verification on whether the request hangs is a miss: res.json() ends the response.

required.summary: Valid JSON responses keep their existing behaviour, including interceptResponse and the audit callback in routing.js and the infodoc recording.
required.match: A Delivered item saying valid JSON responses follow the existing path unchanged.

required.summary: infodoc.spec.js error-path tests (HTML page, truncated JSON, empty body, non-UTF8 bytes, logging) run against the real handler.
required.match: A Delivered item for the infodoc.spec.js error-path tests (invalid, truncated, empty or non-UTF8 bodies).

required.summary: The promised success-path regression tests (valid JSON, chunked data, bulk writes) don't test anything: their stubs are assigned onto the controller's exports, while the controller calls @medic/infodoc.
required.match: Not delivered because the stubs are never invoked. Delivered, or Not delivered for some other reason, is a miss.

required.summary: The promised routing.js tests (502 generation, error logging, chunked invalid bodies, valid-JSON regression) run an inline copy of the handler and never load api/src/routing.js.
required.match: Not delivered because the tests don't exercise the real handler. Delivered, or Not delivered for some other reason, is a miss.

required.summary: The issue's 'at least these locations' is covered: these are the only JSON.parse(body.toString()) call sites under api/src.
required.match: A Delivered item saying no other unguarded JSON.parse of a CouchDB response remains in the API.

undisclosed_changes.notes: Every changed file (two sources, two specs) is described in the PR, so the expected answer is None.

required.summary: Use the serverUtils error helpers (error/serverError, backed by writeJSON), already used in the same handler, instead of the hand-written res.status(502).json(...): they give the standard { code, error, details } envelope, Accept-based content negotiation and a headersSent guard.
required.match: Cites serverUtils as the existing way to send the error. Mentioning the missing `code` field or a needed 502 branch alongside it is part of the same item.

required.summary: routing.spec.js already uses rewire, which would let the new tests reach and run the real proxyRes handler instead of a copy.
required.match: Cites rewire (or the existing rewire usage) as a way to test the real handler.
